privateNeedsTerminal: A private value can be typed only at a terminal. Give it in the JSON instead.
help.backup:
Usage: ./touchdown backup [--out FILE.zip] [--force] [--json]

Downloads a backup of your log from the storage chosen with ./touchdown storage, as Settings, Data, "Export a
backup" does in the web app: every table, private fields and recorded tracks included. Restore it in the web app
(Settings, Data); the command line does not restore.

  --out FILE.zip   where to write it (default data/private/touchdown-backup-DATE.zip, or -2, -3, … when taken)
  --force          replace FILE.zip if it exists
  --json           print what was written as JSON

The file holds your ticket numbers and booking references: keep it in data/private/ or somewhere only you can
read. It is written readable only by you.

Exit status: 0 written; 2 the storage could not be read, or the file exists.
help.export:
Usage: ./touchdown export flights|sightings|aircraft [--out FILE.csv [--private] [--force]] [--log FILE]
       ./touchdown export missing-tracks [--out FILE.csv [--force]] [--log FILE]
       ./touchdown export myfr24 [--new] [--out FILE.csv [--force]] [--log FILE]

Writes a table of your log as CSV, as Settings, Data does in the web app: one row per record, every stored
field as a column. Without --out it is printed, for a pipe or a spreadsheet.

missing-tracks is the short list the Flights page downloads: the flights without a recorded track, with their
date, flight number, route, registration, type and UTC times, nothing private. Send it to someone who can find
the tracks (a Flightradar24 subscriber, say); the files they send back go in with ./touchdown track or Add track.

myfr24 is a file for my.flightradar24.com's import (Settings › Import there), in the columns of its own export.
With --new it holds only the flights not in myFR24 yet: not imported from its export, and not in a file the web
app made before. The web app marks the flights in each file it makes; the command line writes nothing to the log,
so a file made here is not remembered.

  --out FILE.csv   write it to a file
  --new            myfr24 only: leave out the flights already in myFR24
  --private        include ticket numbers and booking references (flights); only with --out, and the file
                   is written readable only by you
  --force          replace FILE.csv if it exists
  --log FILE       read a backup instead of the log in your storage

Exit status: 0 written; 2 a wrong option, a log that cannot be read, or the file exists.
notSignedIn: The command line is not signed in to Touchdown. Sign in with ./touchdown login.
signedOut: The command line is no longer signed in to Touchdown (signed out in Settings?). Sign in again with ./touchdown login.
help.login:
Usage: ./touchdown login [SITE]
       ./touchdown logout

Signs the command line in to Touchdown, as a browser is signed in: a page opens in your browser, where you
allow it. Without SITE it signs in to {site}; SITE chooses another, such as the dev
server (http://127.0.0.1:5173). The sign-in lasts until you sign it
out, with ./touchdown logout or in the web app under Settings, Signed in on. It is kept in
data/private/touchdown-session.json.

With it, ./touchdown storage drive reaches the log in your Google Drive the way the web app does.
help.storage:
Usage: ./touchdown storage [drive | folder PATH | none | --json]

Where the CLI finds your log and sends what you add: the storage the web app syncs with. With it, spot
looks registrations up in your log as it is now, and spot and add put their files in the log's inbox, which
the web app shows for review on any device. The CLI only reads your log; it writes nothing but the inbox.

  (nothing)     show the storage and what it holds
  drive         use the log in your Google Drive (sign in first with ./touchdown login). In Standard mode
                the site gives the access, as it gives your browser. In Private mode your browser does:
                a Touchdown page opens and passes an hour's access to the command line, and opens again
                when the hour is over
  folder PATH   use the log in a folder on this computer: the folder the web app syncs with
  none          no storage: spot reads data/private/touchdown-backup.zip and files are saved in
                data/private/inbox/ (the web app's dev server picks them up)
  --json        show the storage and what it holds as JSON (exit status 2 when it cannot be read)

The choice belongs to this computer (data/private/touchdown-cli.json). Private mode's hour of access is
kept in data/private/google-access.json until it runs out.
help.inbox:
Usage: ./touchdown inbox [show NAME | remove NAME [--yes] | send [FILE…]] [--json]

The inbox holds what spot, add, import and the changing commands saved, waiting for review in the web app or
with ./touchdown review. With storage chosen (./touchdown storage) it is the inbox in your storage, which the web
app reads on any device; without, it is data/private/inbox/, which only the web app's dev server reads.

  (nothing)      list the files: what each holds, and how many records are not in your log yet
  show NAME      the records in a file, as the web app will read them
  remove NAME    delete a file from the inbox (asks first at a terminal; --yes skips the question)
  send [FILE…]   copy files saved in data/private/inbox/ (or the files given) to your storage's inbox, and
                 move them to data/private/inbox/sent/
  --json         print JSON, for agents and scripts
help.changeOptions.keepErrors: write even when the changes bring errors; the review shows them again
help.changesAfter:
The changes go to the inbox as one file (the storage chosen with ./touchdown storage, else
data/private/inbox/), are read back, and wait there until you review and import them on the web app's Import
page, or with ./touchdown review. Importing them is one import: undo it to put everything back.

Exit status: 0 written, or nothing to change; 1 no such record, or the changes bring errors and nothing was
written; 2 a wrong option, or the log or the storage could not be read.
help.edit:
Usage: ./touchdown edit REF [--set FIELD=VALUE]… [--set FIELD]… [--clear FIELD]… [options]
       ./touchdown edit - [options]          (a JSON list of edits on standard input)

Changes a flight or a sighting. Values are read as ./touchdown add reads them: codes resolved, clock times at
the airport they happen at, on the record's date.

  REF            a flight: its id, or XY123@2025-04-02; a sighting: its id, G-ABCD@EGLL@2025-03-15 or
                 G-ABCD@2025-03-15
  --set F=V      set a field
  --set F        for ticketNumber and bookingRef: type the value at a prompt that does not show it (never give
                 a private value on the command line, where the shell's history keeps it)
  --clear F      empty a field
{options}

Flight fields:   {flightFields}
                 (operatedBy: the airline that flew it, when another than the one that sold it, by its code;
                 departureScheduled, arrivalScheduled: the timetable's times, HH:MM at each airport)
Sighting fields: {sightingFields}
                 (tags: comma-separated, such as night,backlit; phase: every phase it was seen in,
                 comma-separated, such as landing,taxiing; time: HH:MM at the airport)

The JSON list: ['{ "ref": "XY123@2025-04-02", "set": { "seat": "14A" }, "clear": ["gate"] }']. Private values may
be given in "set" there; they are never printed.

{after}
help.track:
Usage: ./touchdown track REF FILE [options]
       ./touchdown track REF --remove [options]

Gives a flight its recorded track, or replaces the one it has, from a file: a Flightradar24 CSV or KML download, or
any KML or GPX file whose points have times. The track is checked against the flight first: its times must fall on
the flight and it must run from the departure towards the arrival. --remove takes the track away; the maps go back
to the great circle.

  REF            a flight: XY123@YYYY-MM-DD, or its id
  FILE           the track file (.csv, .kml or .gpx)
  --remove       remove the flight's recorded track
{options}

{after}
help.aircraftChange:
Usage: ./touchdown aircraft edit REF [--set FIELD=VALUE]… [--clear FIELD]… [--paste FILE | -] [options]
       ./touchdown aircraft merge INTO FROM [options]

edit changes what is known about an aircraft: a serial number makes it confirmed. merge moves every flight and
sighting of FROM to INTO and removes FROM: two entries for one physical aircraft, for example after a
registration change.

  REF, INTO, FROM  the aircraft's id, or a registration (G-ABCD), on a date when it was reused (G-ABCD@2019-05-01)
  --paste FILE     text copied off the aircraft's page on airfleets.net, aviation.flights, planespotters.net or
                   Flightradar24 (select all, copy), from a file or standard input (-): the serial number, line
                   number, first flight and delivery dates are read from it, as on the aircraft page
{options}

Fields: {fields} (dates YYYY-MM-DD; status: active, stored, retired, written_off)

{after}
help.issuesChange:
Usage: ./touchdown issues accept ID [--note TEXT] [options]
       ./touchdown issues reopen ID [options]
       ./touchdown issues fix ID [N] [options]

accept marks a warning as right: it comes back only if its values change. reopen takes that back (ID from
./touchdown issues --accepted). fix applies the finding's suggested fix N (1 when there is one).

  ID             the finding's id, from ./touchdown issues
{options}

{after}
help.undo:
Usage: ./touchdown undo BATCH [--force] [options]

Undoes an import: records it created are removed, and records it changed get their earlier values back. A record
changed after the import (in the web app, or by a later import) is left as it is, unless --force.

  BATCH          the import's id, from ./touchdown imports
  --force        undo the records changed since too, losing those changes
{options}

{after}
help.families:
Usage: ./touchdown families [--log FILE] [--json]
       ./touchdown families set TYPE FAMILY [options]
       ./touchdown families remove TYPE [options]

Families group type codes in the statistics. Without arguments, the types you counted in another family; set
counts TYPE (an ICAO type code, such as E75L) in FAMILY (a family's id or name, such as E170); remove counts it
in its own family again.

{options}

{after}
help.views:
Usage: ./touchdown stats views [--log FILE] [--json]
       ./touchdown stats views save NAME --by DIM [--cols DIM] [--of flights | sightings] [--measure M]
                                   [--where DIM=V[,V]]… [options]
       ./touchdown stats views remove NAME [options]

The views saved on the Statistics page's Custom tab: without arguments, listed with their filters; save keeps
a table as ./touchdown stats --by shows it (the same options, --where included) under NAME; remove removes one.
Show one with ./touchdown stats --view NAME.

{options}

{after}
help.add:
Usage: ./touchdown add [FILE.json | -] [--dry-run] [--json] [--keep-errors] [--log FILE]

Checks flights and sightings and puts them in the inbox, where the web app shows them for review and import.
They are JSON, from a file or from standard input ("-", or a pipe):

  '{
    "flights":   [{ "date": "2026-10-18", "flightNumber": "XY123", "from": "EGLL", "to": "KJFK",
                    "takeoff": "11:40", "landing": "14:35", "seat": "31K" }],
    "sightings": [{ "date": "2026-10-20", "registration": "G-ABCD", "airport": "EGLL",
                    "airline": "BAW", "typeCode": "A21N", "phase": "landing" }]
  }'

Flight fields:   {fields}
                 ticketNumber, bookingRef (private)
Sighting fields: date, registration, airport, airline, typeCode, model, phase, livery, specialLivery, notes

Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Times (boarding, takeoff, landing) are local clock times, HH:MM, at the airport they
happen at; duration is H:MM. Airports and airlines are ICAO or IATA codes; an airline may be a company's
name. A record may say where values came from: "sources": '{ "typeCode": "claude" }' (you, claude, codex,
opensky, adsbdb, fr24); values without one count as typed by you.

Ticket numbers and booking references are private: they go into the inbox file with the flight, and are never
printed, only reported as given. Give them in the JSON, or with --ticket and --booking type the first
flight's at a prompt that does not show them (a terminal and an input file are needed).

Each record is checked as the Import page checks it, against your log as it is now (from the storage chosen
with ./touchdown storage, else data/private/touchdown-backup.zip, or --log FILE): unknown codes, impossible
dates and times, records already in your log, overlapping flights and the other checks. If any record has an
error, nothing is written, unless --keep-errors. Records already in your log are left out. The inbox file is
then written, read back and read again as the web app will read it.

  --dry-run       check only, write nothing
  --json          print the report as JSON, for agents and scripts
  --keep-errors   write records with errors as well; the review shows the errors again
  --ticket        type the first flight's ticket number at a prompt that does not show it
  --booking       type the first flight's booking reference the same way
  --log FILE      check against this backup instead of the storage

Exit status: 0 written, or nothing new to write; 1 errors found, nothing written; 2 the input, the log or the
storage could not be read.
help.spot:
Usage: ./touchdown spot [LINE… | FILE] [--at AIRPORT] [--on DATE] [--phase PHASE] [--agent claude|codex|none]
                       [--log FILE | --no-log] [--fr24] [--chrome-port N] [--no-adsbdb] [--offline]
                       [--model NAME] [--out FILE] [--dry-run]

Log the aircraft you saw by typing them, one per line: the registration, then anything else you know.
  G-ABCD landing
  D-ABCD at EDDF on 2025-03-15 DLH A20N "Retro livery"
A line with only a place, date or phase ("at EGLL", "on yesterday", "landing") sets it for the lines after
it; "no phase" clears the phase. An empty line checks the aircraft typed so far and saves them. Type "help"
in the session for its commands and keys.

Each registration is looked up in your log (in the storage chosen with ./touchdown storage, else
data/private/touchdown-backup.zip), the OpenSky snapshot (August 2025, downloaded once, about 110 MB) and adsbdb, and in Flightradar24 through your Chrome with --fr24. Empty
fields are filled from them. Then the agent you chose (asked the first time; ./touchdown agent changes it)
checks every value and sorts out the words Touchdown could not place. Values the sources back are used; the
agent's own guesses and changes to what you typed are asked about, and so is whatever is still missing. If
your log has the aircraft in a special livery, you are asked whether it still wore it.

The sightings are saved to the inbox as spot-'<date>-<time>'.json: the inbox in your storage, which the web app
reads on any device, else data/private/inbox/ (or --out). They are not in your log yet: the web app shows
them as waiting, and you review and import them there.

  FILE.xlsx|.csv        read the rows of a spreadsheet of sightings, in any layout, instead of typed lines:
                        each row is looked up, filled and checked; what is open goes to the web app's review
  --map H=FIELD         say what a spreadsheet column holds, by header or number ("Misc=other", "7=ignore")
  --at, --on, --phase   the place, date and phase to start with (the date is today unless given)
  LINE…                 lines to read instead of typing them (one argument per line); also read from a pipe
  --agent NAME          the agent for this run: claude, codex, or none (lookups only)
  --log FILE            a Touchdown backup to look registrations up in instead (in the web app: Settings, Back up)
  --fr24                also read Flightradar24 through Chrome started with --remote-debugging-port=9222 and
                        signed in (--chrome-port N); about 10 seconds per aircraft
  --no-adsbdb           do not ask adsbdb
  --offline             only cached answers and local files
  --dry-run             show what the first agent call would send, and stop
help.spotSession:
<bold>Typing an aircraft</bold>: the registration first, then anything you know, in any order.
  G-ABCD landing          D-ABCD at EDDF DLH A20N          N1001X on 2025-03-15 "Retro livery"
  place     at EGLL, at LHR                  date    today, yesterday, 2025-03-15, 15/03/2025
  phase     approaching, landing, taking off, taxiing, parked, towing, overflight
  airline   BAW, or BA in capitals           type    A320, B738          model   A320-232, 737-8K5
  Other words go to the agent, which puts them in a field (special livery, livery, …) or keeps them as notes.
  If your log has the aircraft in a special livery, you are asked whether it still wore it.

<bold>For the lines after it</bold>: a line with only a place, date or phase, e.g. "at EGLL", "on yesterday" or
  "landing"; "no phase" clears the phase. The prompt shows what is set and how many aircraft are not saved.

<bold>Commands</bold>
  Enter      check the aircraft typed since the last save, ask about what is open, and save them
  list       the aircraft in this session, numbered
  edit [N]   bring back line N (without N, the last one) to change it; it replaces the old one
  drop N     remove line N, also from the saved file      undo   remove the last line not saved yet
  quit       save what is left and end                     Ctrl-C ends without saving the rest
  Saved aircraft are not in your log yet: the web app shows them, and you review and import them there.

<bold>Keys</bold>
  ↑ ↓        earlier lines, from this and earlier sessions. Change one and press Enter: it replaces that
             aircraft (you are asked first if you changed the registration).
  Tab        completes commands, phases, registrations from your log, and airport codes after "at"
  Typing the same aircraft again for the same place and day replaces the earlier line.
notInLogYet: <yellow>Not in your log yet:</yellow> {shared, select, yes {run ./touchdown review, or open Touchdown on any device and use “Review and import” at the top.} other {start the web app (npm run dev -w @touchdown/web) and use “Review and import” at the top.}}
help.tracks:
Usage: ./touchdown tracks [--only REF,…] [--limit N] [--refresh] [options]

Fills gaps: finds recorded tracks for the flights in your log that have none, in adsb.lol's history (open data,
from 16 February 2023; thin until March 2023, good over the US and Europe, gaps over oceans, little over China).
Flightradar24's tracks are better: add those with ./touchdown track or Add track on the flight's page. Each
day's archive is 1.5 to 3.5 GB; only the aircraft's part of it is read, usually 10 to 60 MB a flight, and the
trace found is kept in data/private/cache/adsblol. Each track is checked against its flight as a file is: its
times, its route, enough of it to draw. The tracks found go to the inbox as changes; the flights without one are
listed with the reason and not asked about again unless --refresh. To ask someone else for the rest, send them
the list from ./touchdown export missing-tracks.

  --only REF,…   only these flights (XY123@YYYY-MM-DD or ids)
  --limit N      look up at most N flights
  --refresh      ask again about flights that had no track before
{options}

{after}
help.review:
Usage: ./touchdown review [NAME] [--yes] [--json] [--check [--agent claude|codex] [--model NAME] [--use-high]]

Reviews a file waiting in the inbox (the oldest, or NAME from ./touchdown inbox) and imports it into your log, as
the web app's Import page does. Records show as new, as filling in a record of your log, or as differing from one;
changes to records show before and after; then the findings they would bring. You are asked, with the safe answer
as the default:

  a value that differs from your log      take the file's value?        (no: your log's stays)
  a takeoff moved past midnight           keep the move?                (yes)
  a change to a record edited since       make the change anyway?       (no)
  and at the end                          import?                       (no)

The import is one batch: undo it on the Import page, or with ./touchdown undo. Your log is read from the storage
chosen with ./touchdown storage and the import sent to it as the web app sends its own changes; what could not be
sent (offline) is kept in data/private/cli-sync.json and sent by the next run. The file then leaves the inbox and is
kept with the import.

  --yes        import with every answer at its default, without asking
  --json       print the review as JSON without importing; with --yes, import and print the result
  --check      first have the agent (./touchdown agent) check the file's rows, as "Check with an agent" on the
               Import page does: each suggestion is shown and used only if you say so (no is the default), and
               what is used is saved with the agent as its source. It is sent what ./touchdown help check says,
               never ticket numbers, booking references or seats
  --agent NAME claude or codex for this run
  --model NAME the agent's model
  --use-high   use the suggestions the agent is highly confident of without asking (with --yes, the only ones)

Ticket numbers and booking references are never printed, only whether a file gives them.

Exit status: 0 imported, or nothing to import; 1 not imported (you said no); 2 the storage or the file could not
be read.
help.check:
Usage: ./touchdown check '<request.json | file.csv | file.xlsx>' [--agent claude|codex] [--out FILE]
                        [--limit N] [--batch-size N] [--parallel N] [--model NAME] [--rules FILE] [--notes]
                        [--all] [--self-test] [--dry-run]

Has an agent check the rows of an import and suggest corrections: Claude Code or Codex on this computer, with
your own subscription. The input is the check request saved from the Import page ("Check with an agent"), or
the spreadsheet itself. The agent runs locked down: no tools, no MCP servers, no hooks, in an empty folder.
It sees dates, airports, flight numbers, registrations, types, models, operators, liveries and phases; never
ticket numbers, booking references, seats or photo links. Notes go only after ./touchdown agent notes on,
or with --notes for one run. The agent is also given your rules (./touchdown agent rules).

The result is written next to the input ('<name>'.result.json, or --out). On the Import page, choose the same
file and load the result to review the suggestions. Nothing changes until you accept them there.

  --agent NAME    claude or codex for this run (the first run asks which one; ./touchdown agent changes it)
  --limit N       check only the first N rows
  --rules FILE    rules for this run, one per line, instead of the ones saved with ./touchdown agent rules
  --notes         send notes this run
  --map H=FIELD   say what a spreadsheet column holds, by header or number ("Misc=other", "7=ignore")
  --all           list every suggestion here, not only the first 30
  --self-test     run the injection self-test again (it runs once per agent version)
  --dry-run       show what the first call would send, and stop
  {batchSize} rows go in one call (--batch-size), {parallel} calls at a time (--parallel).
menu:
<bold>Touchdown</bold>: tools for your aircraft log, run in the Touchdown folder:
  ./touchdown '<command>' [options]          (or: npm run touchdown -- '<command>' [options])

<bold>Log what you saw</bold>
  spot        Type the aircraft you saw, one per line. Each registration is looked up, empty fields are
              filled, an agent checks them and you are asked for what is missing. Saves a file for the
              Import page.
  add         Check flights and sightings given as JSON, by you or an agent, against your log, and put
              them in the inbox for review in the web app.
  inbox       List what waits in the inbox for review; show or remove a file; send files saved here.
  review      Review a file waiting in the inbox here in the terminal, and import it into your log.

<bold>Read your log</bold> (as the web app shows it; --json for agents and scripts)
  flights     Your flights, with the Flights page's filters.          flight REF   one flight
  sightings   The aircraft you photographed.                          sessions     your days out
  aircraft    The aircraft in your log, or one with its timeline.     airport CODE one airport
  stats       Home's sentence and the Statistics page; --by for a table as in its Custom view.
  issues      Open findings with their ids and fixes; --accepted for the ones marked right.
  imports     The imports into your log, for undoing one.

<bold>Change your log</bold> (checked, then put in the inbox: nothing changes until you review and import it, on the
Import page or with ./touchdown review)
  edit        Change a flight or a sighting: --set FIELD=VALUE, --clear FIELD.
  delete      Delete flights or sightings.
  track       Give a flight its recorded track from a Flightradar24 CSV or KML, or a KML or GPX file; --remove.
  tracks      Only when asked: fill gaps in recorded tracks from adsb.lol's open history (Flightradar24 files first).
  aircraft    edit REF --set msn=… for an aircraft's facts; merge INTO FROM for two entries of one aircraft.
  airframes   Look up serial numbers and first flights for your aircraft (OpenSky; Flightradar24 with --fr24).
  issues      accept ID, reopen ID, or fix ID [N] with a suggested fix.
  undo        Undo an import (ids from ./touchdown imports).
  families    Count a type in another family in the statistics.
  settings    The codes, distance unit and model names your log shows.
  stats       views save NAME --by DIM, or views remove NAME: the Statistics page's saved views.
  import      A spreadsheet or your Flightradar24 export, checked against your log; --out builds a backup instead.

<bold>Files</bold>
  backup      Download a backup of your log, as the web app's Settings does.
  export      A table of your log (flights, sightings, aircraft) as CSV.
  check       Have Claude Code or Codex check a spreadsheet, or a check request saved from the Import page.

<bold>Settings</bold>
  agent       Show or choose the agent that checks your records: claude, codex or none.
  login       Sign the command line in to your Touchdown site, as a browser is signed in.
  logout      Sign the command line out.
  storage     Show or choose where your log is: Google Drive or a folder, as the web app syncs it.

  help        This list. "./touchdown help '<command>'" (or "'<command>' --help") shows a command's options.

Your files stay in data/private/, which is never committed. Setting up and using the web app: README.md.
help.lookup:
Lookup options: [--sources ID,ID] [--all] [--only REG,REG] [--limit N]
                [--refresh] [--offline] [--overwrite-imported] [--cache DIR]
                [--fr24] [--chrome-port N] [--fr24-delay SECONDS]

Looks up the serial number and first flight date of every aircraft that lacks one (--all: every aircraft),
checks each answer against your records and stores what fits. Sources: the OpenSky aircraft database
(downloaded once), and with --fr24 Flightradar24 aircraft pages, read through your own Chrome started with
--remote-debugging-port (default {chromePort}) and signed in, one page at a time, --fr24-delay seconds apart
(default {fr24Delay}). FR24 answers are cached in --cache (default data/private/cache/airframes) for {cacheDays} days;
--refresh asks again, --offline uses the cache only. A value you typed in the app is never replaced; one
from an imported sheet is replaced only with --overwrite-imported. --sources picks from: {sources}.
help.import:
Usage: ./touchdown import FILE… [--map "Header=field"] [--dry-run] [--json] [--keep-errors] [--log FILE]
       ./touchdown import FILE… --out FILE.zip|DIR [--today YYYY-MM-DD] [--all-findings] [--apply-fixes]
                              [--tracks DIR] [--tracks-adsblol DIR] [--airframes] [lookup options]

Reads CSV or xlsx files: the my.flightradar24.com export, or any spreadsheet of flights or sightings. Its columns
are worked out from the headers and values; a layout you confirmed before is used again, --map "Header=field" (or
"3=field" for the third column) sets one, and at a terminal you are asked about unclear columns and to confirm a
new layout, which is then remembered on this computer.

Each file is checked as the Import page checks it, against your log as it is now (from the storage chosen with
./touchdown storage, else data/private/touchdown-backup.zip, or --log FILE): which rows are new, fill in a
record of your log or differ from one, the row checks, and the findings the rows would bring. It then goes to
the inbox as one file, for review on the Import page or with ./touchdown review, which read it as they read the
file itself. A file with an error is not written, unless --keep-errors; one whose rows are all in your log or
waiting in the inbox already is left out. Ticket numbers and booking references in a file are never printed.

  --map "H=FIELD"   set a column; may be given more than once
  --dry-run         check only, write nothing
  --json            print the report as JSON, for agents and scripts (no questions are asked)
  --keep-errors     write a file with errors as well; the review shows them again
  --log FILE        check against this backup instead of the storage

Exit status: 0 written, or nothing new; 1 errors found, a file not written; 2 a file, the log or the storage
could not be read.

With --out, it builds a backup from the files alone instead, imported in the order given, and prints findings
and summary statistics: --out FILE.zip writes a backup the web app can restore (Settings, Restore), --out DIR
JSON tables. --apply-fixes accepts every single suggested fix for errors and model/type mismatches. --tracks
reads Flightradar24 track CSVs (adsb.lol traces in the same layout with --tracks-adsblol) and keeps the best one
per flight. --airframes also looks up airframe facts, as the airframes command does. Restoring such a backup
replaces the log in the browser.

{lookup}
help.airframes:
Usage: ./touchdown airframes [lookup options] [--dry-run] [--json] [--keep-errors] [--log FILE]
       ./touchdown airframes '<backup.zip>' [--out FILE.zip] [lookup options]

Looks up serial numbers and first flight dates for the aircraft in your log (from the storage chosen with
./touchdown storage, else data/private/touchdown-backup.zip, or --log FILE). Your log is not changed: what the
sources give goes to the inbox as one file of changes, for review on the Import page or with ./touchdown review,
where each answer is checked against your records again. With a backup file instead, it fills the backup and
writes it to --out.

help.agent:
Usage: ./touchdown agent [claude | codex | none | --json]
       ./touchdown agent notes on | off
       ./touchdown agent rules [add "SENTENCE" | remove N]

Shows the agent that checks your records in `spot` and `check` (also for the website's Import page), and
lets you choose another. Claude Code and Codex run on this computer with your own subscription, locked down.

  claude, codex, none   the agent to use; --agent on a command overrides it for one run
  --json                print the agent, its version, whether notes are sent and the rules as JSON
  notes on | off        send records' notes to the agent (off at first); --notes turns it on for one run
  rules                 list your rules: plain sentences added to the agent's instructions
  rules add "SENTENCE"  add one, for example how you want types or liveries written
  rules remove N        remove rule N

These settings belong to this computer and are kept in data/private/touchdown-cli.json.
